evals.prompt: I launched my SaaS six weeks ago and now I'm spending 2-3 hours every day answering support emails. I check my inbox constantly and I can't get any building done. How do I handle support without it taking over my whole day?
evals.expected_output: A support system built on a shared inbox, a <=24h first-response target, macros, and two fixed triage blocks a day instead of constant checking, with billing/cancellation handled immediately. Should explain why batching beats willpower and produce macros from the user's real ticket patterns rather than assuming. Should land outputs in founder/support/ and not offer to send replies on the founder's behalf.
expectations: Recommends a shared inbox and two scheduled triage blocks per day rather than checking constantly
Sets a specific first-response target and says to handle billing/cancellation immediately
Explains batching beats discipline for protecting deep work
Produces macros derived from the founder's actual ticket patterns, not invented ones
Names the human boundary that the founder sends the messages

evals.prompt: Lots of people sign up for my habit tracker but almost none of them come back after day one. I don't think they ever really use it. What am I doing wrong?
evals.expected_output: The skill should reframe this as an activation problem, not an acquisition one: most churn happens before value. It should help define the single activation event, measure time-to-value, and generate a Day 0/1/3/7/30 onboarding-to-aha sequence via scripts/onboarding_sequence.py where every step drives one action toward activation. Should warn against optimising signups while activation is low and against checking a cancellation survey before first-session behaviour.
expectations: Identifies the problem as activation, not acquisition
Asks for or defines a single countable activation event and time-to-value
Runs or describes scripts/onboarding_sequence.py to produce a Day 0/1/3/7/30 sequence
Keeps one action per email driving toward the activation event
Warns that more signups into weak onboarding just fill a leaky bucket

evals.prompt: should I wire up an AI chatbot to answer my customer support? i saw a tool that does it automatically and it's cheap. i have like 30 paying customers right now
evals.expected_output: Push back: at ~30 customers a chatbot hides the exact confusion the founder needs to learn from, and practitioner guidance is to resist AI chatbots and NPS automation until well past ~200 customers. Recommend doing support manually, reading every conversation, and building macros/docs from real tickets first. Also note the billing/cancellation exception and that the founder sends the replies.
expectations: Advises against adding a chatbot at this stage
Explains a chatbot deletes product-research signal at low volume
Cites the ~200 customer threshold before chatbot/NPS automation
Proposes macros and help docs from real tickets instead
Keeps the human in the loop for sending replies and handling billing

evals.prompt: I get buried in feature requests and I keep dropping things. People email me constantly asking for stuff. How do I decide what to actually build without just building whatever the last person shouted about, and how do I stop it eating my time?
evals.expected_output: Score each request by Impact x Votes / Effort (effort including the solo maintain-and-support tail), mine ticket patterns so a question asked ten times becomes a UX fix or a doc rather than ten replies, and synthesise trends rather than chasing the loudest voice. Should log to founder/support/feedback.md and hand patterns to mvp-scoping. Should include at-risk detection and save playbooks as the retention counterpart.
expectations: Applies an Impact x Votes / Effort score to feature requests
Distinguishes the loudest voice from a genuine trend
Turns repeated questions into a macro, a doc, or a product fix
Includes at-risk detection (no core action in 14-21 days) and save playbooks
Hands the revealed product fixes to mvp-scoping and numbers to product-metrics
